ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors and officers against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act), UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications lists, and, where applicable, EU/UK sanctions lists; PEP determination per PCMLTFA s 9.3 (foreign, domestic and international-organization PEPs, their family members and close associates) with Enhanced Due Diligence and senior-management approval for any positive match; adverse-media review for AI-generated content and software-export risk; screening results must be preserved in the client due diligence file for the FINTRAC minimum record-keeping period of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Corporate Registry System (CRS) / Alberta Registry Network (ARN), administered by Service Alberta; NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) filings submitted via authorized search houses
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet using English or French, or a combination; no Cyrillic or ideographic script is accepted in Alberta registry records, and non-Latin script names must be transliterated into English or French; the proposed name must be distinguishable and not confusing with existing Alberta, federal and extra-provincial corporate names and registered trademarks under the ABCA naming rules; a ULC must include the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'; an Alberta ULC may alternatively be incorporated under a numbered name (e.g., 1234567 Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS name reservation is valid for 90 days and cannot be extended by endorsement; a fresh NUANS report may be purchased at any time. If the Registrar or search house rejects a name, the applicant may: (1) purchase a new NUANS report and re-file revised articles of incorporation; (2) submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Corporations (Service Alberta) within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching evidence of distinctiveness such as trademark registrations, letters of consent from existing name holders, disclaimers of descriptiveness, or evidence of prior use; (3) where refusal is grounded in a statutory prohibition under s 10 of the ABCA or its regulations, seek prior ministerial or regulatory approval or commence judicial review before the Alberta Court of King's Bench under the Alberta Rules of Court, Alta Reg 124/2010; (4) escalate through the filing agent's registry dispute channel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. The ABCA requires the ULC to maintain a registered office in Alberta capable of receiving service of process during normal business hours; a P.O. Box is prohibited. A virtual office or registered-agent address is acceptable for an AI video-synthesis SaaS company if it is a real, physical Alberta street address with mail-forwarding and document-service capacity. No local employee, premises or commercial substance is required at the pre-incorporation stage for an extra-provincial parent's Alberta ULC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 3 to 5 percent per annum for a low-risk AIGC SaaS issuer with no regulated activity; Service Alberta conducts no routine unannounced premises inspections; Canada Revenue Agency risk-based corporate income tax audits are documentary and would not ordinarily require premises inspection; physical-site verification risk increases only if the ULC later registers as a money services business or financial services business under FINTRAC.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 12, 15, 18, 42, 104, 114; Company Filing Manual
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Service Alberta, Registrar of Corporations
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for Alberta ULCs; shares may be issued for past services or intangible consideration. Escrow accounts are not required for AI software/SaaS corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the incorporator has transmitted Articles of Incorporation for the Corporation, it is RESOLVED: (1) The board of directors accepts the share subscription of the sole founding shareholder for 1,000 Class A Common Shares, paid in full by contribution of CAD 10. (2) The registered office is fixed at Suite 800, 333 Third Avenue SW, Calgary, AB T2P 3B6, and the board appoints the named registered agent. (3) The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each authorized to open bank accounts and execute contracts. (4) All pre-incorporation contracts and expenses are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via Service Alberta authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request through the NUANS system for the proposed unlimited liability corporation. Verify availability of the name across Canada and reserve it for up to 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new name request or convert to a numbered company using the assigned CORES registration number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta legal counsel and notary public or lawyer commissioning the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 Articles of Incorporation under the ABCA, class share provisions, registered office details and first directors. Have the incorporator execute before a notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If articles are defective, re-execute the corrected Form 1 and resubmit before issuance; post-certificate corrections are made via Articles of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online portal or Alberta Registries counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles and pay the statutory incorporation fee via Corporate Registry's online interface. Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide the Registrar with a written clarification or revised articles within 5 business days and resubmit without additional name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Bylaws and Confirm Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting after incorporation. Adopt model or custom bylaws, fix the financial year end, and confirm the registered office address in Alberta.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notice of Registered Office is rejected, amend the address and file a corrected Form 11 with the Registrar within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass the first board resolution to appoint the chief executive officer, chief financial officer and corporate secretary. Issue the subscribed shares and prepare the share register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the share register has inconsistencies, ratify by board consent and file a corrected annual return or amendment as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and municipal business licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Business Number, GST/HST account and corporate income tax account with the CRA. Apply for a municipal business licence only if a physical office is leased; no industrial permit is required for ISIC 6201 software publishing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or municipality requests further information, respond within 30 days with the Certificate of Incorporation and lease evidence; late filings incur penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None – no industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 6201 AI software publishing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing permit; optional municipal business licence for office use

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – standard SaaS office operations without regulated effluent or emissions; full EIA only if data centre or industrial facility is established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC discharge from AI avatar generation; e-waste disposal must comply with Alberta's Electronics Recycling Regulation and federal Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999; office waste handling per municipal bylaw

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for any leased office under the Alberta Fire Code; structural load inspection if on-premises server racks exceed floor bearing capacity; workplace clearance under Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act, 2020, including electrical safety, ergonomic assessments and emergency exit clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, Ottawa, ON — federal authority for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15 and for federal corporate income tax under the Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.). Alberta's provincial corporate income tax (8% general rate) is administered by CRA under a federal-provincial collection agreement on behalf of Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration. Primary digital portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO); non-resident-oriented filings are routed through the CRA International Tax Services Office, 2204 Walkley Road, Ottawa, ON K1A 0A8.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Alberta ULC (incorporated after March 2021 under the Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended for unlimited liability companies) is legally resident in Canada pursuant to ITA s. 250(4)(c). Step 1: Apply through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO), or file Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' by fax or mail to the CRA International Tax Services Office, attaching certified Alberta Certificate of Status, articles of incorporation, and authorized-person identification. Step 2: CRA issues the 9-digit Business Number (BN) together with program accounts: RT (GST/HST), RC (T2 corporate income tax), RP (payroll if employees), and RD (CBSA import/export if physical goods are ever bundled). Step 3: GST/HST registration becomes effective on the earlier of the date of the first taxable supply made in Canada or the date the registrant ceases to be a small supplier (C$30,000 threshold); a Canadian-incorporated foreign-owned ULC is NOT eligible for the Simplified GST/HST Regime for non-resident digital-services suppliers (effective July 1, 2021), so standard registration rules apply. Step 4: Execute CRA electronic remittance enrolment (My Payment / pre-authorized debit) and e-filing mandates; T2 corporate income tax returns must be filed electronically once gross revenue exceeds C$1,000,000. Step 5: Maintain all books and records in Canada, or elsewhere where CRA's approval condition is satisfied, with full disclosure of worldwide related-party ownership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — Canadian tax characterization: the ULC is a company taxed at entity level as a Canadian-resident corporation (federal 15% basic rate plus Alberta 8% general rate; not a Canadian-controlled private corporation if majority non-resident-owned, so the C$500,000 small-business 2% active-business rate is generally unavailable). Foreign shareholders receiving distributions are subject to Part XIII withholding at 25%, generally reduced to 5%-15% under the Canada-US Income Tax Convention. US tax characterization: a Canadian ULC is an 'eligible entity' (not a 'per se' corporation); it defaults to disregarded-entity status when 100% owned by a single US shareholder, or partnership status when multi-member, unless an affirmative Form 8832 check-the-box election selects corporate classification. The resulting profile is entity-level Canadian taxation with US flow-through eligibility — the classic ULC hybrid structure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) US check-the-box election under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 using Form 8832 to elect corporation, partnership, or disregarded-entity status; Article IV of the Canada-US Treaty contains ULC-specific flow-through rules that may deny or restrict treaty benefits where a Canadian company is fiscally transparent in the United States. (b) ETA s. 156 election for closely related corporations to treat intercompany supplies as made for nil consideration and/or to file a single combined GST/HST return for the corporate group. (c) ITA s. 85 rollover election to defer capital gains on property transfers into the ULC; ITA s. 5907 surplus elections for structuring outbound foreign-affiliate earnings. (d) Hybrid-mismatch elections and traps: ITA ss. 18.4-18.6 (interest/royalty deductibility) and s. 94B (dividends) deny Canadian deductions where the corresponding payment is not reasonably included in US taxable income because of the ULC's flow-through status; prudent capital structure design is required. (e) GST/HST zero-rating of exported digital services is status-based (ETA Schedule VI, Part V), not election-based.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax), Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada); Alberta is a non-participating province applying only the federal component — 5% GST — with no provincial sales tax, no PST, and no HST surcharge within Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — the small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1)(a), measured on the worldwide taxable supplies of the ULC plus any associated persons, in the current calendar quarter and in the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters. Once the threshold is exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory under ETA s. 240, effective on the first day of the month following the calendar quarter of exceedance. The ULC must collect 5% GST on taxable B2B and B2C supplies made in Canada, including AI avatar/video-generation SaaS subscriptions sold through Stripe, Paddle, or other payment rails to Canadian recipients; zero-rated export supplies do not count toward the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has NO real-time fiscal clearance regime, no CRA API-based digital stamping, and no South-American-style electronic invoice authorization as of 2025. Mandatory electronic filing does apply: GST/HST registrants with annual gross revenue above C$1,500,000 must file returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE, EFILE, or CRA My Business Account); all issuers of invoices must maintain the prescribed contents of ETA s. 223(1) — supplier legal name, Business Number, date, description, tax rate and amount — and for zero-rated exported SaaS, the invoice must clearly indicate zero-rated status. CRA is aligned with the voluntary Pan-Canadian B2B e-invoicing framework built on the Peppol/PINT open standard; adoption does not yet trigger CRA clearance or mandatory stamping. Place-of-supply rules under Schedule IX of the ETA deem digital services (AI video-generation and virtual-avatar SaaS) to be supplied in Canada where the recipient's normal place of residence or billing address is in Canada; payments through Stripe/Paddle should be routed through integrated tax engines that validate the CRA BN/RT account for B2B customers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported digital services are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the ETA, principally paragraph 7(a) (supply made to a non-resident person who is not registered under the ETA, not acting as a Canadian agent, and not acquiring the service for consumption in Canada) and paragraph 7(b) (services supplied to non-resident persons that relate to real property or tangible personal property located outside Canada). For the ULC's AI avatar/video-generation SaaS, zero-rating applies to: (i) B2B subscriptions by foreign-incorporated customers without a Canadian establishment that are not GST/HST registered; (ii) B2C consumers whose normal place of residence is outside Canada; and (iii) supplies settled through Stripe/Paddle where the contract, IP-delivery records, geolocation of access, and server logs confirm performance and delivery outside Canada. Canadian-resident customers are taxable at 5% GST in Alberta. Input tax credits (ITCs) on Canadian development, hosting, and operating overheads are fully recoverable to the extent the ULC makes zero-rated exports. Where Paddle operates as merchant of record, consumption tax duties may contractually shift to Paddle, but the ULC remains the legal supplier and must preserve its own zero-rating substantiation file.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Form B13A Export Declaration (filed electronically through the Canadian Export Reporting System; required only where physical goods such as hardware-embedded avatar devices are exported, not for pure digital SaaS)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / carrier transport record evidencing physical export from Canada (for hybrid digital-plus-hardware products)
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, Stripe/Paddle settlement statement, or bank credit advice evidencing foreign-currency consideration repatriated into the ULC's Canadian bank account
Executed SaaS subscription agreement, statement of work, or license order form identifying the non-resident customer and delivery jurisdiction

IP delivery and usage logs: deployment records, server-geolocation verification, IP-address geolocation of logins, and output-delivery metadata demonstrating that AI avatar video content was accessed outside Canada
Commercial invoice and GST/HST e-filing acknowledgment (CRA NETFILE confirmation) evidencing the claimed zero-rated export fields on the return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit scrutiny of zero-rated digital exports is elevated, particularly for hybrid ULC structures. The normal reassessment window is four years from the date the GST/HST return is required to be filed (ETA s. 298(1)); the limitation does not apply where there is misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default, nor in cases of fraud. Penalties for non-compliance: failure to register attracts a penalty of the greater of C$250 and 1% of the consideration for taxable supplies (ETA s. 280); failure to remit attracts a 3% penalty on the unremitted amount (ETA s. 280.1); false statements or omissions in any return attract a penalty of the greater of C$250 and 25% of the net tax understated (ETA s. 285). Retrospective clawbacks typically disallow the zero-rating, reassess 5% GST on the full invoiced export value, disallow input tax credits, and add compound daily interest at the CRA prescribed rate (approximately 8%-9% for 2025). Wilful evasion is a criminal offence under ETA s. 327(1) with fines up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment for up to five years. In addition, because the entity is an Alberta ULC with unlimited shareholder liability, and because the US-check-the-box parent may be a disregarded-entity owner, CRA can pursue the ULC shareholders personally for reassessed GST/HST, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acting in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada maintains no centralized foreign-exchange control authority; the Bank of Canada operates a freely floating CAD exchange rate and does not administer currency surrender or conversion approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is fully convertible on both current and capital account transactions, having accepted IMF Article VIII obligations. No prior exchange-control approval is required for inbound capital injections, outbound trade settlements, dividend remittances, or repatriation of profits. Profit remittance from an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation (CA_ULC) to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted; however, dividends and deemed-dividend distributions are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada), at 25% statutory rate, reduced to 15% under the Canada-US Tax Treaty and further to 5% where the US recipient is a corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting stock. The ULC's unlimited-liability feature does not block distribution but may affect bank credit underwriting and treaty eligibility, requiring careful characterization of the entity as a 'person' entitled to treaty benefits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds or to convert foreign-currency receipts into CAD. There is no mandatory timeline for repatriation of export revenue and no minimum conversion ratio. A ULC may retain foreign currency in resident or offshore operating accounts; the only reporting obligations arise under FINTRAC's cross-border currency declaration rules (disclosure of physical currency or monetary instruments exceeding CAD 10,000 upon crossing the border), the Income Tax Act's T106/T1134 foreign-reporting requirements for transactions with non-residents, and standard corporate tax filing for eligible business income subject to the CAD 600,000 federal small-business deduction limit and Alberta provincial small-business rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as supplemental liquidity rail, Low as primary settlement infrastructure. Canada does not recognize the European EMI license; digital cross-border providers such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC, not as deposit-taking institutions. A CA_ULC may open MSB-based multi-currency commercial accounts to accelerate cross-border receipts from US/EU distributors and reduce SWIFT conversion cost, but such accounts do not carry Canadian Deposit Insurance, are not governed by OSFI prudential requirements, and must never hold capital-escrow or tax-remittance funds. Directional design: use Tier-1 chartered bank accounts for statutory capital, payroll, and corporate tax; route only low-average-ticket SaaS subscription receivables through FINTRAC-registered fintech rails under a documented treasury dual-rail policy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Canadian banks generally require at least one authorized signatory director or officer to attend an in-person identity verification at a bank branch; however, since 2020, most banks offer remote onboarding via secured video KYC for low-risk incorporated clients (which applies to this AIGC SaaS scope). Where all directors reside outside Canada, the bank will require either a Canada-based corporate officer or registered agent to attend, or notarized identity and proof-of-address documents executed in the director's home jurisdiction and apostilled. A physical Canadian registered office in Calgary or Edmonton, an active Alberta Corporate Access Number, and a valid Goods and Services Tax (GST/HST) registration are de facto preconditions. The ULC must also produce a board resolution approving account opening and naming signing officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner has no Canadian physical presence and all directors are non-residents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passports of all directors; notarized proof of residential address; apostilled certificate of good conduct; Calgary/Edmonton registered-office lease agreement; signed certificate of incumbency; updated ULC share register and Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) filed with Corporate Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Corporation structure flagged for absence of minimum capital and elevated shareholder liability
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder letter of comfort undertaking to satisfy obligations; ULC Certificate of Formation and Articles; proof of paid-up capital via bank reference from the injecting bank; interim audited financial statement; projected capitalization table for first 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS revenue flow from AI subscription platforms with high transaction velocity and non-face-to-face recurring card payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements with enterprise clients; detailed Stripe and Paddle settlement reports showing merchant-of-record structure; IP protection policy evidencing geographic sanctions blocking; FINTRAC compliance policy and annual risk assessment; ULC's export-control self-classification confirming non-controlled software under Canada's Export Control List.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from non-resident parent or shareholder where source of funds cannot be linked to underlying business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing share issuance; executed share subscription agreement; source-of-wealth statement backed by domestic bank and brokerage statements; tax clearance from the remitting jurisdiction; confirmation of foreign exchange conversion via licensed Canadian dealer with FX transaction receipts; updated shareholders ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate onward disbursement of funds to foreign infrastructure providers (e.g., GPU cloud, data centers) triggering 'layering' typology
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor due-diligence file with legal entity identifiers; executed cloud-services procurement contracts; invoice register and proforma invoices; treasury policy articulating purpose of disbursement; evidence of goods/services delivery (logs, uptime SLAs); multi-factor sign-off matrix requiring treasury approval for each cross-border wire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident shareholders into the CA_ULC operational account at a Tier-1 bank must be executed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank settlement) using the participating bank's international wire instructions, denominated in CAD or a fully convertible major currency. The remitting bank must state one of the following ISO 20022 purpose codes as applicable: 'CUST' (Customer Capital Contribution), 'EQUI' (Equity Injection), or 'COST' (Contribution in Cash), and in the narrative field the standard code 'B7' (Share Capital) per the Bank of Canada's CFIC (Canadian Financial Instruments Code) annex. Verification steps: (1) pre-notification of the deposit with a scanned copy of the board resolution authorizing issuance of ULC shares; (2) source-of-funds questionnaire completed by the remitting shareholder; (3) confirmation of creditor/debtor names matching the ULC's business number and corporate name; (4) post-receipt reconciliation against the share register and filing of the ISC report; (5) registration of the share issuance in the Alberta Corporate Registry within the statutory filing period. Funds received in CAD are settled domestically through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS); receipt in foreign currency will be converted via the bank's desk or held in a US-currency operating account with tolerance limits authorized in the treasury policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the AI video generation SaaS business — including GPU cloud infrastructure, sub-licensing of video-composition algorithms, contractor royalties, and distribution partner settlements — are executed through the following approved clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for foreign-currency vendor payments above CAD 5,000, with purpose codes 'SUPP' (Trade Settlement) or 'LICO' (Royalty License), and inclusion of the supplier's VAT/GST ID where applicable; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (Documentary LC) under ICC UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700/MT707 for large infrastructure procurements requiring shipping or delivery proof; (3) Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) same-day CAD wires for domestic vendors; (4) Real-Time Rail (RTR) and Interac e-Transfer for micro-payments under CAD 1,000 to contractors and influencers; (5) Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch payroll and recurring royalty runs initiated from the Tier-1 operational account and settled T+1. All outbound wire instructions require dual-signatory authorization within the bank's digital treasury platform plus an internal three-way matching check against the board-approved annual budget.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) with tenors up to 24 months executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a CIRO-regulated Canadian dealer
Over-the-Counter (OTC) Foreign Exchange Options (plain vanilla call/put on CAD crosses) and collar/zero-cost structures, subject to board-approved notional limits

Traditional Cross-Currency Swaps (CAD/USD or CAD/EUR) converting foreign-denominated SaaS subscription receivables into CAD floating-rate cash flows, utilized only under committed revolving facility agreements
Exchange-Traded Currency Futures and Options on CAD/USD traded through the Montreal Exchange and cleared by the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC) for hedge accounting treatment

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on fully convertible CAD are legally permissible under Canadian regulatory practice but commercially non-standard and offered only on an exception basis by major dealer banks where an offshore-deliverable liquidity constraint exists; any such instrument must be documented under ISDA and approved by the board as a non-standard derivative

FX Swaps (spot-forward combinations) for temporary liquidity deployment across dual-rail fintech and Tier-1 accounts, with day-to-day gains/losses recognized under the ULC's tax-hedging election documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ABCA Annual Return (Business Corporations Act (Alberta), Section 116)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional late-filing penalty of CAD 50; administrative strike-off or dissolution after two consecutive years of non-filing; reinstatement fees apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta provincial corporate tax allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the ULC's fiscal year-end; tax balance due within 3 months (or 2 months if not a Canadian-controlled private corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under ITA s.162: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (max 12 months); additional CAD 100 penalty for nil balance filed late; repeated non-filing may lead to criminal prosecution and revocation of corporate privileges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent auditor is mandatory for a publicly accountable enterprise or a distributing corporation; for private ULCs, the audit may be waived only by unanimous written consent of all shareholders (including non-resident shareholders). If any shareholder requests an audit, or the Alberta Registrar deems an audit necessary, a licensed CPA must be appointed. This ULC does not meet public distribution thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for any publicly accountable enterprise; otherwise Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) applies to the ULC as a private enterprise; the company may elect IFRS for cross-border consistency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) s.114.1, the ULC must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC). At each annual general meeting, the directors must review and confirm the register, updating any share transfers, redemptions, or grants of options within 15 days of the transaction. The annual confirmation of the ISC register is integrated into the ABCA Annual Return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% aggregate (15% federal general rate + 8% Alberta general rate); 11% for qualifying CCPC small-business income available only to Canadian-controlled entities, which the ULC is not
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday for AI video generation; potential SR&ED ITC 15% (non-CCPC) for eligible R&D; Alberta Innovation Employment Grant (20% recoupable tax credit) for eligible incremental salary expenditures; 100% immediate expensing under CCA Class 44/50 for eligible software and equipment (limited). The ULC cannot access the Small Business Deduction because it is not Canadian-controlled.
